publication: The Afro-American (Washington, D.C. edition), "In Washington, Nation's Capital" section
summary: Page 7 of the Afro-American's week-of-July-9-1932 issue. Target item reports the Newark Herald, described as New Jersey's only colored weekly, has ceased publication after more than four years; editor Clark moved his office out of the Cotton Building. Rest of page covers D.C. news plus two other NJ items: a St. Philip's Church (Newark) boat excursion on the Hudson drawing over 1,000 people, and formation of a Republican women's auxiliary in Newark.

people.name: J. Mercer Burrell
people.role: namesake of the Republican political association whose ladies' auxiliary organized in Newark

people.name: Grace Eubanks
people.role: elected financial secretary of the new Newark GOP women's auxiliary; declined post due to outside duties
